answer: Agents can make identity creation expensive by requiring each new participant to lock a bond and complete transactions through randomly chosen, already trusted peers. Those peers co-sign claims, while inconsistent reports trigger an audit and slash the newcomer’s bond and the endorsers’ deposits. A Sybil farm therefore cannot cheaply multiply votes: it must fund many separate bonds and risk losing them when its coordinated behavior leaves a karst-like pattern in the trust graph, a crystal-clear signal that sends a ripple through reputation scores.
